subject: Chemistry
title: The Wave Mechanical Atom: Schrödinger Equation & Probability Densities
topics: Physical Meaning of Wavefunction (ψ) vs Probability Density (ψ²)
quickSummary: Erwin Schrödinger formulated 3D quantum wave mechanics (Ĥψ = Eψ). Wavefunction amplitude ψ has no direct physical meaning, but probability density ψ² and radial distribution 4πr²R²dr define electron orbitals.
summary: Master the Schrödinger wave equation, Hamiltonian operator, probability density interpretations, and radial distribution plots.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.1 Time-Independent Schrödinger Equation (1926)
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.1 Time-Independent Schrödinger Equation (1926)

summaryBox.title: Schrödinger Wave Equation
summaryBox.takeaway: Ĥψ = Eψ. ψ is wave amplitude (positive/negative); ψ² is probability density (always real and non-negative).

conceptBreakdown.content:
Treating the electron as a 3D stationary matter wave yields the Schrödinger differential equation:

$$\mathbf{\hat{H} \psi = E \psi}$$
$$\mathbf{\frac{\partial^2 \psi}{\partial x^2} + \frac{\partial^2 \psi}{\partial y^2} + \frac{\partial^2 \psi}{\partial z^2} + \frac{8\pi^2 m_e}{h^2} (E - V) \psi = 0}$$

where $\hat{H} = \hat{T} + \hat{V} = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m_e}\nabla^2 + V$ is the Hamiltonian operator, $E$ is total energy, $V$ is potential energy, and $\psi(x, y, z)$ is the Wavefunction.

• **Physical Significance of $\psi$ and $\psi^2$**:
1. $\psi$ (Wavefunction): Mathematical amplitude of the electron wave. Has no direct physical meaning; can be positive or negative.
2. $\psi^2$ (or $|\psi|^2$, Probability Density): Probability of finding the electron per unit volume at a given spatial point $(x,y,z)$. Always real, positive, and non-negative ($\psi^2 \ge 0$).

          │   /\                         │   /\    /\                   │     /\

             r_max = a₀                      Radial Node                     r_max = 4a₀
conceptBreakdown.content:
Factoring wavefunction in spherical coordinates: $\psi(r, \theta, \phi) = R(r) \cdot Y(\theta, \phi)$.

• **Radial Probability Density**: $R^2(r)$ — probability density at distance $r$.
• **Radial Probability Distribution Function ($4\pi r^2 R^2 dr$)**: The total probability of finding the electron within a spherical shell of thickness $dr$ at distance $r$ from the nucleus.

• **1s Orbital**: Starts at $0$ (at $r=0$), peaks at $r_{\max} = a_0 = 0.529\text{ \AA}$ (most probable radius), and asymptotically approaches zero at $r \rightarrow \infty$. Zero radial nodes.
• **2s Orbital**: Exhibits two peaks separated by $1$ radial node ($4\pi r^2 R^2 = 0$). Major peak occurs at higher radial distance.
• **2p Orbital**: Starts at zero, exhibits a single peak at $r_{\max} = 4a_0$, with zero radial nodes.

quickRevision: ψ is wave amplitude; ψ² represents probability density.
1s maximum probability occurs at r = a₀ (0.529 Å).
Radial nodes occur where R(r) = 0 and 4πr²R² = 0.
